topic: Natural Language Processing: Transformers, Attention, and Tokenization

questions.scenario: An enterprise legal-tech firm deploys a standard Multi-Head Attention (MHA) Transformer model on an NVIDIA A100 (80GB) cluster to process complex contracts averaging 16,000 tokens per document. During concurrent batch inference, the system repeatedly encounters GPU Out-Of-Memory (OOM) errors. Profiling reveals that intermediate activation memory scales quadratically with sequence length due to storing the full attention weight matrices ($N \times N$) in High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), causing severe memory bandwidth bottlenecks.
questions.question: Which algorithmic technique should the engineering team adopt to eliminate intermediate attention matrix materialization in GPU HBM and compute exact attention with $O(N)$ memory overhead without quality loss?
options: A) FlashAttention, utilizing GPU SRAM tiling and online softmax computation to calculate exact attention in a single fused kernel
B) Linformer, utilizing low-rank linear projections to compress Key and Value sequences into a fixed dimension $k$
C) Longformer, combining local sliding window attention with task-specific dilated global attention patterns
D) Reformer, replacing dot-product attention with Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH) to group keys and queries into shared chunked buckets
questions.correct_answer_text: A) FlashAttention, utilizing GPU SRAM tiling and online softmax computation to calculate exact attention in a single fused kernel
questions.explanation: FlashAttention avoids materializing the massive $N \times N$ attention matrix in high-latency GPU High Bandwidth Memory (HBM). By leveraging GPU on-chip SRAM tiling and an online softmax algorithm (tracking running normalization factors), it computes exact (non-approximated) attention while reducing memory access overhead from $O(N^2)$ to $O(N)$ with respect to sequence length, resolving the memory bandwidth bottleneck.

questions.scenario: A cross-border banking system processes customer queries across English, Devanagari (Hindi), and code-mixed vernacular scripts. When deploying a standard Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenizer trained on an unweighted general web crawl, engineers notice 'token inflation': an identical semantic sentence requires 18 tokens in English but over 92 tokens in Hindi. This causes rapid context window saturation, high latency, and degradation of self-attention representations for non-Latin inputs.
questions.question: What is the primary root cause of this token inflation, and what is the standard industrial mitigation during tokenizer training?
options: A) Under-segmentation caused by character-level fallback; mitigate by replacing BPE with non-deterministic WordPiece tokenization.
B) Pre-tokenizer regex misconfigurations stripping whitespace; mitigate by switching to strict Unicode NFKC normalization prior to tokenization.
C) Under-representation of non-Latin corpora in the training split; mitigate by employing script-stratified oversampling and setting explicit per-script vocabulary allocations.
D) High morphological inflection in Devanagari; mitigate by applying stemming and lemmatization to text prior to passing strings to the subword tokenizer.
questions.correct_answer_text: C) Under-representation of non-Latin corpora in the training split; mitigate by employing script-stratified oversampling and setting explicit per-script vocabulary allocations.
questions.explanation: Token inflation occurs when the training corpus for frequency-based subword tokenizers (like BPE or SentencePiece Unigram) heavily skews toward English/Latin text. Infrequently observed scripts fail to merge character sequences into meaningful subwords, fragmenting words into single Unicode characters or individual bytes. The industrial solution is temperature-based upsampling or stratified sampling of minority language corpora and enforcing dedicated vocabulary token budgets during tokenizer training.

questions.scenario: A real-time financial fraud surveillance pipeline employs a Transformer backbone pre-trained with Absolute Learned Positional Embeddings up to a context window of 2,048 tokens. During high-frequency trading bursts, transaction dependency chains extend to 6,000 tokens. When engineers evaluate these longer inputs by linearly interpolating the positional indices, the model's perplexity explodes, and attention distributions degrade into near-uniform noise across tokens.
questions.question: Which positional embedding strategy should be integrated to enable seamless length generalization beyond the pre-training window while maintaining token distance sensitivity without requiring full model retraining?
options: A) Learnable 1D Fourier Embeddings, combined with linear extrapolation of position IDs beyond the maximum pre-trained range.
B) Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE), combined with NTK-aware (Neural Tangent Kernel) scaled frequency interpolation.
C) Absolute Sinusoidal Embeddings, combined with greedy sliding-window attention masks over the extended sequence.
D) Absolute Scaled Embeddings with zero-padding vectors for indices exceeding 2,048 tokens.
questions.correct_answer_text: B) Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE), combined with NTK-aware (Neural Tangent Kernel) scaled frequency interpolation.
questions.explanation: Absolute learned embeddings fail to extrapolate beyond the maximum trained index because the model has never optimized weights for those positions. Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) encodes relative position by rotating query and key representations in complex vector space. When scaling context, Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK)-aware scaling interpolates high-frequency dimensions less and low-frequency dimensions more, preserving high-frequency local neighbor information while compressing long-range relative distances, enabling out-of-distribution sequence length generalization.
